description.en: CAIR Nepal HeritageGraph ontology merged with the LUX (Yale Linked Art / CIDOC-CRM) interoperability bridge.

definition.value: Event of transferring responsibility for temple maintenance, ritual performance, or artifact stewardship
Event of creating an architectural structure, murti, or paubha
Event of evaluating the physical state of a heritage object or structure
Individual person who performs, commissions, documents, or verifies heritage activities
Physical objects created by human activity
Method or craft process used in production or ritual
General actor (person or group) responsible for events
A physical condition state of a heritage object
Temporal extent of an event or period
Defined geographic location where events occur and structures exist
Physical substance used in construction or crafting
Event that destroyed or damaged a structure.

A provenance-bearing belief or claim about a heritage entity or event. The assertion is represented as CRMinf I2 Belief and as a prov:Entity, allowing source, attribution, generation time, revision, confidence, and reconciliation status to be recorded explicitly.
Direct LinkML representation of prov:Activity. Applied to events and processes that use, transform, generate, document, assess, or verify entities.

Direct LinkML representation of prov:Agent. Agents bear responsibility for activities or entities. PROV-O permits an individual agent also to be typed as an Entity, but does not define every Agent as a subclass of Entity.

Direct LinkML representation of prov:Entity. Applied to physical, digital, conceptual, and assertion-bearing things that participate in provenance relations. PROVENANCE SCOPE (alpha.5 design decision): for classes whose instances are real-world referents (structures, deities, places, actors), the provenance slots (was_derived_from, was_attributed_to, was_generated_by, generated_at_time) describe the DATA RECORD about the referent, not the referent itself -- a stupa is not generated by the survey that records it. Referent-level history is modelled through events (Production, DestructionEvent, etc.). RDF deployments SHOULD carry record-level provenance in named graphs or on InformationObject/Assertion nodes.

comment.value: Title transfer (vs. custody only). LUX alias: 'Acquisition'.

definition.value: Candidate must be within the prescribed pre-pubescent age range.
Carved or constructed component of an architectural structure (e.g., Gajur, Torana, Tundal)
Physical structures built for religious, social, or civic purposes. Links to events of production, use, custody, and documentation.
A vocabulary of architectural styles for South Asian heritage, mapped to CIDOC E55 Type.
Government or institutional administrative record
Any HeritageGraph entity or event that may be the subject of an assertion.

comment.value: Generic super-class above HeritageAssertion / Verification / SyncreticRelationship. LUX alias: 'AttributeAssignment'.
Generic existence-start event when no specific Production/Birth/Formation applies. LUX alias: 'BeginningOfExistence'.
Birth event of a Person; carries timespan, place, and parent attributions. LUX alias: 'Birth'.

definition.value: Calendar reckoning system with conversion rules for multi-calendar temporal reasoning
Hereditary social group (Jati) with specific ritual roles and occupational duties
Buddhist votive shrine (chaitya); votive stupa form found across the Kathmandu Valley.
Festival involving ceremonial chariot procession (e.g., Rato Machhindranath Jatra)
Controlled vocabulary for the physical condition of heritage objects and structures.
Ritual event that transforms an object into a sacred vessel (e.g., Prana Pratistha for Murti)

Root container for cultural heritage data instances. PLACEMENT RULE: put each instance in the most specific collection available (e.g. a Festival in festivals, not ritual_events; a Person in persons, not actors); broader collections exist for instances of the general classes only.

comment.value: LinkML container construct; no LUX equivalent. Treated as a structural InformationObject for navigation.
Formally curated holding (museum collection, library set). LUX alias: 'CuratedHolding'.
Conservation / inventory / accession activities by a museum or Guthi. LUX alias: 'CurationActivity' → crm:E87.
Monetary unit referenced in Acquisition/Payment activities. LUX alias: 'Currency'.

definition.value: Institution or person currently responsible for stewarding heritage data.
Original source from which heritage information was derived
Controlled vocabulary for the temporal precision of recorded heritage dates.

comment.value: Death event of a Person. LUX alias: 'Death'.

definition.value: Divine conceptual entity in Hindu, Buddhist, or syncretic traditions. Distinct from physical representations (Murti) and ritual presences.
Pilgrim lodge operated by a Guthi organization
Stone spout (hiti) with carved imagery, used for ritual bathing and daily water supply

comment.value: Photographs, 3D scans, audio recordings. LUX alias: 'DigitalObject' (note: LUX uses CRMdig dig:D1, not crmdig:).
Height/width/depth/weight values. LUX alias: 'Dimension'.
Termination event of a Guthi/Group. LUX alias: 'Dissolution'.

definition.value: Activity that records information about a heritage entity or event and may generate information objects or assertions. It aligns CIDOC CRM documentation practices with prov:Activity.

comment.value: Field encounter / rediscovery of a heritage object. LUX alias: 'Encounter' → CRMsci sci:S19_Encounter_Event (NOT crm:E87 Curation Activity).
Generic existence-end event (mirror). LUX alias: 'EndOfExistence'.

definition.value: Event of installing a deity's murti or symbol within a temple sanctum
Controlled vocabulary for whether a heritage structure still exists physically.

The 'fearlessness test' popularly described (animal heads, masked dancers in darkness). Its historical and contemporary practice is DISPUTED -- some former Kumaris contest how it is described. Represented as an assessment whose accounts are source-attributed via has_assertion, NOT as a mandatory criterion.
Large-scale community ritual event (Jatra) involving processions, music, and collective participation
The activity of measuring, photographing, or assessing a site in person.
The structured data or report resulting from a field survey.

comment.value: Founding event of a Guthi/Group. LUX alias: 'Formation'.
Generic group of actors. Super-class of Guthi and CasteGroup.

definition.value: Endowed trust organization unique to Nepal, managing temples, rituals, and land through hereditary or voluntary membership
Controlled vocabulary of Guthi functional types (CRM E55_Type)
Major event affecting heritage structures or ritual life (earthquake, epidemic, political transition, fire, flood).
Candidate's horoscope must be compatible with the city and ruling authority.
Sacred visual art objects that depict or embody deities through iconographic conventions

comment.value: Catalogue numbers, DANAM IDs, DOIs. LUX alias: 'Identifier'.

definition.value: A recorded piece of information about heritage

comment.value: Inscriptions on stone/metal/manuscripts. LUX alias: 'Inscription'.

definition.value: Ritual installing a selected girl into the Kumari role and residence, activating the tenure (distinct from selection, which chooses her, and retirement, which ends it).
God-house residence of a Kumari during tenure (e.g., Kumari Ghar, Kathmandu). Specialised ReligiousStructure.

Abstract event that bounds a KumariTenure (selection, enthronement, or retirement). Each concrete subclass requires exactly one tenure edge via slot_usage: initiated_tenure (selection), ended_tenure_of (retirement), or bounds_tenure itself (enthronement).
Ritual or administrative event that formally ends a Living Goddess tenure, returning the person to secular status. Common triggers: first menstruation, injury causing blood loss, serious illness.

The role/office of Kumari (living-goddess embodiment) that a person assumes for the duration of a KumariTenure. The role is the type; the tenure is the time-bounded holding of it; the person is the holder.

Tantric ritual process of selecting a new Living Goddess from eligible candidates. Involves examination of 32 auspicious physical marks (lakshana), horoscope matching with the city and ruling authority, and tests of fearlessness (e.g., remaining calm among buffalo heads and masked dancers in darkness). Performed by committee of Vajracharya priests, royal priest (Raj Jyotish), and astrologer.

Time-bounded role where a person embodies a deity as Living Goddess (Kumari), residing at a specific god-house and supported by religious institutions. This class captures the unique Nepali tradition of living deity embodiment in young girls selected from Buddhist Shakya/Vajracharya families.

comment.value: Language of a Name or LinguisticObject (Devanagari, Nepali, Newari, Sanskrit, English). LUX alias: 'Language'.

Things subject to legal frameworks — e.g. 'Ancient Monument' under Nepal heritage law. LUX alias: 'LegalObject'. (HG previously called this 'LegalConcept' which is not a Linked Art class; renamed for compatibility.)

definition.value: Candidate must belong to an eligible lineage (Shakya / Vajracharya Newar Buddhist family).

comment.value: Textual content — inscriptions, manuscripts, transcribed oral history. LUX alias: 'LinguisticObject'.

definition.value: Festival featuring masked dancers embodying deities (e.g., Kartik Naach)

comment.value: Act of measuring an object's dimension. LUX alias: 'Measurement'.

definition.value: Dataset metadata information

comment.value: Restoration or alteration of a Murti/Temple/artifact. LUX alias: 'Modification'.
Amount of money. LUX alias: 'MonetaryAmount'.
Physical movement of an object — distinct from custody change. LUX alias: 'Move'.

definition.value: Consecrated statue of a deity, ritually activated to serve as divine presence (not merely depiction)

comment.value: Multilingual name. LUX alias: 'Name' → crm:E33_E41_Linguistic_Appellation (multi-instantiated).

definition.value: The interaction event between a researcher and a knowledge holder.
The recording or transcript of an oral history interview.
Open-air pavilion for resting travelers
Traditional Newari scroll painting (thangka) with mandala and deity iconography

comment.value: Generic historical period (Lichhavi, Malla, Shah, Rana). LUX alias: 'Period'.

definition.value: Union of the tangible heritage classes: architectural structures, iconographic objects, and standalone architectural elements. Used as the range of slots that apply to any physical heritage thing (production, custody, condition assessment).
Candidate must have an unblemished body with no scars, wounds, or loss of blood/teeth.
Pond or tank for water storage, ritual bathing, and ecological management

A single machine-readable proposition (subject - predicate - object) held true by an Assertion. Modelled as a singleton proposition set (CRMinf I4); the predicate is a URI/CURIE, the object either a heritage entity or a literal.

comment.value: Abstract works, doctrines, beliefs — separate from any physical carrier. LUX alias: 'PropositionalObject'.

Wrapper for chains of custody / ownership / movement events. LUX models this as crm:E7_Activity classified_as a 'provenance' Type — NOT a separate la: class. Migration: LUX provenance activities land here as crm:E7_Activity instances.

definition.value: Architectural structure whose defining purpose is religious: enshrines a deity and/or is a locus of ritual activation. Abstract grouping for sacred structures across traditions (temple, stupa, chaitya).
Religious or philosophical tradition (e.g., Hindu, Buddhist, Syncretic)
Community structures for travelers and pilgrims, maintained by Guthi organizations

comment.value: Access/IP rights on photographs and datasets. LUX alias: 'Right'.

definition.value: A performed assessment carried out during Kumari selection. Modelled as an event (not a hard criterion) so that source-specific, possibly conflicting accounts of whether/how it was conducted attach as provenanced Assertions rather than being asserted as fact.
Intentional ritual activity that activates sacred space, invokes deities, and binds social groups
Controlled vocabulary of ritual and festival activity types in Kathmandu Valley living heritage.
Multi-story rest house (3-5 floors) with ritual and social functions
An eligibility criterion a candidate must satisfy to assume the Kumari role. Modelled as explicit subclasses so 'what are the eligibility criteria?' is a subclass query, not free text.

comment.value: Curated grouping. LUX alias: 'Set' — this is one of the genuine la: classes (la:Set), not a CRM class. Linked Art deliberately mints la:Set distinct from crm:E78_Curated_Holding to allow ad-hoc groupings.
Linked Art mints la:Set distinct from crm:E78 to allow ad-hoc groupings. Within HG we additionally treat Set as a CuratedHolding for navigation; no semantic collapse — both parents remain.

definition.value: Buddhist dome-shaped reliquary shrine with circumambulation and ritual activation (e.g., Boudhanath, Swayambhunath).

Formalizes the syncretic equivalence between divine entities across different theological frameworks. Following CIDOC CRM E13, it treats syncretism as a propositional claim with associated epistemic authority and provenance.
Controlled vocabulary for kinds of syncretic theological relationships between deities.

Religious structure characterized by deity enshrinement and ritual activation. Legal designation (e.g. 'Ancient Monument' under Nepal law) is recorded per-instance via a governance assertion, not as a class criterion.
Candidate must exhibit the battis lakshana (thirty-two perfections/auspicious bodily marks).

comment.value: Titled name of a work or object. LUX alias: 'Title'.

definition.value: Process of cross-checking heritage claims against multiple sources

comment.value: Iconographic content separate from the physical Murti/Paubha. LUX alias: 'VisualItem'.
